title: Access ahead of Habit
story: Anika arrived early to claim the window seat, then gave it up when she saw Luis used it to follow the board. From the back she missed two formulas and copied them from his notes. Their tutor noticed the swap and asked why. Anika said access mattered more than habit. The tutor left seating open, provided nobody treated a chair as property.

vocabulary.definition: To take something as if it were yours
Mathematical statements written on the board
An exchange of one place or thing for another
The chance to reach or see what is needed

quiz.question: Why had Luis been using the window seat?
options: He used it to follow the board
He wanted to copy Anika’s notes
He had bought the chair as property
He arrived later than the rest of the class
quiz.correctAnswer: He used it to follow the board
quiz.explanation: Anika gave up the seat when she saw he used it to follow the board.
quiz.supportingSentence: Anika arrived early to claim the window seat, then gave it up when she saw Luis used it to follow the board.

quiz.question: What did Anika miss while sitting at the back?
options: Two formulas
The tutor’s question about the swap
Her claim on the window chair
Notes from a different class
quiz.explanation: From the back she missed two formulas and later copied them.
quiz.supportingSentence: From the back she missed two formulas and copied them from his notes.

quiz.question: What did Anika’s reply reveal about her move?
options: Luis seeing the board mattered more than her usual seat
The tutor had ordered her to the back before class
She hoped to hide the formulas she had missed
She believed each chair should be private property
quiz.correctAnswer: Luis seeing the board mattered more than her usual seat
quiz.explanation: Saying that access mattered more than habit shows she gave up her usual seat so he could see.
quiz.supportingSentence: Anika said access mattered more than habit.

quiz.question: What does claim mean at the start of the passage?
options: To take the seat as though it were hers
To complain about the writing on the board
To copy formulas from a classmate
To close the seminar before the end
quiz.correctAnswer: To take the seat as though it were hers
quiz.explanation: She arrived early to claim the window seat, meaning to take it for herself.
quiz.supportingSentence: Anika arrived early to claim the window seat, then gave it up when she saw Luis used it to follow the board.

quiz.question: Why does the writer include the condition about property?
options: To show the tutor allowed choice but not ownership of seats
To prove Luis had purchased the window chair
To explain why two formulas were hidden
To argue that notes can replace the board
quiz.correctAnswer: To show the tutor allowed choice but not ownership of seats
quiz.explanation: Open seating with nobody treating a chair as property sets choice without ownership.
quiz.supportingSentence: The tutor left seating open, provided nobody treated a chair as property.
